name: Short-Term Residence Permit (Kısa Dönem İkamet İzni)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a dwelling used as a house valued at least $200,000, and the property must not be located in a designated 'closed' neighbourhood where foreign-resident concentration exceeds 20%.
requirements.fix_path: Acquire qualifying property outside a closed neighbourhood.

requirements.blocker_text: This covers scientific research, business/commercial connections, on-the-job training, student exchange, tourism, medical treatment, judicial/administrative stay, and Turkish-language courses (max twice) — a documented purpose is required.

evidence_required.document: Property valuation and title deed (property group), or documentation of the specific qualifying purpose (other group)
Health insurance and declared Turkish address

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years each time (investors and TRNC citizens up to 5 years)

sources.title: Residence Permit Types - Presidency of Migration Management

notes: FORMULA VALUE, distinctly separate from tr_citizenship_by_investment's $400,000 real-estate threshold: this residence-ONLY property route requires only $200,000 and yields residence, not citizenship — the clearest and most consequential figure-conflation risk in the entire Turkey dataset, since both are property-based and easily confused. GENUINE, VOLATILE GEOGRAPHIC RESTRICTION: the Ministry of Interior lowered the foreign-resident concentration cap from 25% to 20% effective 1 July 2022, and the Presidency of Migration Management raised the closed-neighbourhood count to 1,169 mahalles across 62 provinces at that time; more recent reporting (single-source, not independently confirmed at tier-1 precision) suggests most closures were reversed by mid-2026, leaving Istanbul's Fatih and Esenyurt as notable remaining closures. This restriction is modeled as a hard requirement here but is explicitly flagged as dynamic — re-verify against the live PMM closed-neighbourhood list before relying on this for any specific location. pr_after_months (96) reflects the standard 8-year Long-Term Residence clock; citizenship_after_months (60) reflects the independent 5-year ordinary-naturalisation clock, which in Turkey does NOT require holding long-term residence first — a genuine structural feature shared with Japan among the countries in this dataset.
